biography: Vernon L. Adams Sr. was born in 1899. He was the son of John H. Adams (1860–1931) and Chessie Fitchett Adams (1860–1939).
Vernon married Florence Melson Webster, daughter of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. Their children included Vernon L. Adams Jr. and Kenneth W. Adams.

The 1930 United States Federal Census records Vernon and Florence living in Baltimore, Maryland, with their son Vernon and Florence's younger brother Eugene Lee Webster. Vernon's parents, John H. and Chessie Adams, were recorded in a nearby household.

The 1940 census records Vernon, Florence, their sons Vernon Jr. and Kenneth, and Eugene Webster in the family household. The 1950 census records Vernon, Florence, Kenneth, and Eugene together in Baltimore.
Vernon died in 1974. He was buried at Moreland Memorial Park in Parkville, Maryland, where he shares a grave marker with Florence.

Addie Leola Daniel was born on August 18, 1881, on Deals Island in Somerset County, Maryland. Her parents were James Daniel and Mary C. Wilson, both identified on Addie's 1922 death certificate as natives of Somerset County. FamilySearch research identifies them more fully as James Fairfax Daniel Sr. (1855–1927) and Mary Catherine Wilson (1859–1910). Addie grew up in a large Daniel family that reportedly included six siblings.

Addie married William Gabriel Snead Webster (1871–1939). FamilySearch records list their marriage as December 24, 1899, in Somerset County, Maryland, although the original marriage record has not yet been examined. The 1900 United States Federal Census records Snead Webster, age 27, and his wife Addie, age 18, living in Tangier District, Somerset County. The census gives Addie's birth as March 1882, differing from the August 18, 1881, date recorded on her death certificate.

Addie and Snead had seven known children: Maynard Snead Webster (1900–1959), Susie Catherine Webster Kramer (1902–1993), Florence Melson Webster Adams (1904–1979), Charles Daniel Webster (1909–1960), Mary Catherine Webster Jackson (1916–1995), James Wilson Webster (1920–2005), and Eugene Lee Webster (1921–1998). The family lived in Somerset County during the early years of their marriage and later established their home in Baltimore, Maryland.

Historical land records document Addie's involvement in property transactions on Deals Island. On August 20, 1906, Lazarus B. Wilson and his wife Annie B. Wilson conveyed land to Addie L. Webster for $250. Family-tree research identifies Lazarus Benjamin Wilson (1857–1922) as Addie's maternal uncle, the brother of her mother Mary Catherine Wilson. On May 12, 1909, Snead and Addie Webster conveyed land to Talmage D. Mister for $575. The later deed refers to property previously conveyed to Addie by Lazarus Wilson in 1906.

By the early 1920s, Addie and her family were living in Baltimore. Her death certificate records that she had resided in the city for approximately eight years and identifies her residence as 2602 East Fayette Street. Her death announcement in The Baltimore Sun appears to give the address as 2202 East Fayette Street, a discrepancy that remains to be resolved.

Addie died on April 26, 1922, in Baltimore, Maryland, at the age of 40 years, 8 months, and 8 days. Her death certificate identifies the cause as chronic myocarditis, a disease of the heart muscle, and names her husband, Gabriel S. Webster, as the informant. Funeral services were held on April 28, 1922, followed by burial at Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore. Her gravestone bears the inscription 'ADDIE L. WEBSTER, 1881–1922, MOTHER.'

Addie's death left several of her children still young, including Eugene Lee Webster, who was an infant at the time. Later federal census records show Eugene living with his older sister Florence and her husband Vernon L. Adams in 1930, 1940, and 1950. Family accounts describe the challenges faced by the Webster family following Addie's death, although the precise circumstances of the children's living arrangements during the intervening years remain under investigation.

James Fairfax Daniel Sr. was born on September 25, 1855, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. Family research identifies his parents as James Travers Daniel (1830–1902) and Louisa Elizabeth Rowe (1835–after 1870). A historical marriage register records the marriage of James T. Daniel and Louisa E. Rowe on January 6, 1855. James Fairfax Daniel's 1927 death certificate identifies his mother as Louisa Thomas, creating a discrepancy with the surname Rowe that remains under investigation.

James married Mary Catherine Wilson (1859–1910), and family research identifies them as the parents of seven children, including Addie Leola Daniel (1881–1922). FamilySearch records their marriage date as December 16, but gives conflicting years of 1875 and 1876. The correct marriage year remains to be established from the original record.

James and Mary Catherine raised their family on Deal Island, Somerset County, Maryland. The 1900 United States Census records their household, including several of their children. Their daughter Addie later married William Gabriel Snead Webster (1871–1939), connecting the Daniel and Webster families.

In September 1902, James F. Daniel was named among the jurors selected from Tangier District for the October term of the Somerset Circuit Court. A newspaper article titled 'Somerset Jurors' listed him alongside three other men from the district, providing additional evidence of his connection to the Deal Island area during this period.

The 1922 Baltimore death certificate of Addie L. Webster identifies her father as James Daniel and records his birthplace as Somerset County, Maryland. This provides documentary evidence supporting Addie's relationship to the Daniel family.

The 1910 United States Census records James Fairfax Daniel as a retail oyster dealer living on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. The census lists him as the head of a household that included his wife, Mary C. Daniel, and three children: James F. Daniel Jr., Annie W. Daniel, and Wilson B. Daniel. His occupation reflects the importance of the oyster trade to the maritime economy of Deal Island during the early twentieth century.

Mary Catherine died in 1910. James later resided in Baltimore, Maryland, although the date of his relocation has not yet been established. His death certificate identifies him as widowed and records his occupation as watchman.

James died on November 26, 1927, in Baltimore, Maryland, at the age of 72 years, 2 months, and 1 day. His death certificate records his birth date as September 25, 1855, and identifies his father as James Daniel and his mother as Louisa Thomas, reflecting the conflicting maternal surname found in this record.

A death notice published in The Baltimore Sun on November 27, 1927, reported that James died at the residence of his daughter, Mrs. Annie W. Drake, at 22 Rueckert Avenue in the Hamilton neighborhood of Baltimore. The notice identified him as the beloved husband of the late Mary C. Daniel. His death certificate independently confirms 22 Rueckert Avenue as both his residence and place of death.

Funeral services were announced for Sunday, November 27, 1927, at 2:30 p.m., at his daughter's residence. The obituary announced interment at Deals Island, Maryland, on Monday afternoon, November 28. His death certificate records a burial date of November 27, 1927, creating a discrepancy between the two records. His gravestone is located at Saint John's Cemetery on Deal Island, where his wife Mary Catherine Wilson Daniel is also buried. The name 'Deals Island' reflects a historical form of the community's name, also remembered in family recollections.

Bette Ann Kramer is the daughter of Adam Johannes Krämer and Susie Catherine Webster Kramer. She appears with her parents and brother Robert in the 1940 United States Federal Census in Baltimore, Maryland.

death_place: Greenville, Pitt County, North Carolina, United States
biography: Robert Adam Kramer was born on November 5, 1936, in Baltimore, Maryland, the son of Adam Johannes Kramer and Susie Catherine Webster Kramer. He was recorded as Robert A. Kramer, age three, in the 1940 United States Federal Census. He died on October 3, 2012, in Greenville, Pitt County, North Carolina.

Adam Johannes Krämer was born on December 8, 1903, in Germany. His 1928 Declaration of Intention identifies his birthplace as Schweinfurt, while his 1942 World War II draft registration records Würzburg. His surname was generally written Kramer in American records.

Adam immigrated to the United States in 1926. According to his Declaration of Intention, he departed from Bremerhaven, Germany, aboard a vessel whose name appears to be Derfflinger, arriving in New York on or about September 29, 1926. He identified Laufach, Germany, as his last foreign residence. By April 1928, Adam was living at 937 South Kenwood Avenue in Baltimore, Maryland, and working as a seaman. According to family history, he initially lived with the family of his aunt Louise Kramer, who had married John Christopher Smearman. Louise's daughter, Charlotte 'Lottie' Smearman, is remembered in family history as the person who introduced Adam to his future wife, Sue Webster.

Adam married Susie Catherine Webster, known as Sue, on July 27, 1929, in Ellicott City, Howard County, Maryland. Their marriage was performed by H. D. Stewart of Emory Methodist Episcopal Church. According to family history, Adam and Sue were introduced by Lottie Smearman, identified as the daughter of Adam's aunt Loise Kramer. They had two children, Robert Adam Kramer and Bette Ann Kramer.

On May 19, 1932, Adam became a naturalized citizen of the United States in the United States District Court for the District of Maryland in Baltimore. His Certificate of Citizenship, No. 3523010, includes his photograph and signature.

According to family history, Adam and Sue purchased a home in Dundalk, Baltimore County, Maryland, in 1938. Their residence at 6902 Brentwood Avenue is documented on Adam's 1942 World War II draft registration and in his 1969 death notice. The family also appears in the 1930, 1940, and 1950 United States Federal Censuses.

Adam's 1942 draft registration identifies his employer as Baltimore Pure-Rye Distilling Company, located on Sollers Point Road in Baltimore. His maritime career is further documented by a United States Coast Guard Merchant Marine officer license issued on June 13, 1953, in Baltimore. The license qualified him to serve as Second Assistant Engineer of Steam Vessels of any horsepower upon any waters. The surviving license does not identify the individual ships on which he served.
Around 1946, Adam Johannes Kramer was treated for tuberculosis at the Maryland Tuberculosis Sanatorium in Sabillasville, Frederick County, Maryland, where he spent approximately a year and a half.

The sanatorium, which opened in 1908, was located in the mountains of northern Frederick County. Its elevation and climate were considered beneficial for tuberculosis patients, and the facility included patient pavilions, medical buildings, dining facilities, and a working farm.

According to the recollections of Adam's daughter, who was born in 1938 and remembers being approximately eight years old at the time, his extended stay occurred around 1946. The precise dates of his admission and discharge have not been established.

Adam died on December 1, 1969, at the age of 65. His death notice identifies his residence as 6902 Brentwood Avenue in Dundalk and names his wife, Sue Webster Kramer, and their children. Funeral services were scheduled for December 4, 1969, followed by interment at Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore, Maryland.

Anna Elizabeth Webster, known as Lizzie, was born on January 19, 1868, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. She was the daughter of Gabriel Snead Webster (1822–1871) and Susan A. Windsor (1843–1911), who married on December 20, 1865. Her 1940 Maryland death certificate identifies her parents as Snead Webster and Susie Windsor, both born on Deal Island.

Anna was the older sister of William Gabriel Snead Webster (1871–1939). Their father died in 1871, when Anna was approximately three years old. Their mother subsequently married William Jacob Webster (1836–1910).

Anna married Major Carroll Todd Sr. (1868–1944), who was born on February 4, 1868, in Dorchester County, Maryland. Their marriage date has not yet been established. Anna's death certificate identifies Major Carroll Todd Sr. as her husband and lists Ira Todd of Crisfield as the informant.

Anna lived in Crisfield, Somerset County, Maryland, during the later years of her life. Her death certificate records her residence as Maryland Avenue and states that she had lived in Crisfield for 22 years. Her occupation was recorded as housework.

Anna Elizabeth Webster Todd died on July 9, 1940, in Crisfield, Maryland, at the age of 72. Her death certificate records burial on July 11, 1940. She was buried at Sunny Ridge Memorial Park in Crisfield, where her husband, Major Carroll Todd Sr., who died on January 22, 1944, is also buried.

Charles Daniel Webster was born in 1909, the son of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. He was recorded as Charles D. Webster, age nine months, in the family's 1910 United States Federal Census household in Somerset County, Maryland. He died in 1960.
Eugene Lee Webster was born in 1921, the son of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. He died in 1998.

Florence Melson Webster was born on March 23, 1904, in Maryland, the daughter of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. She grew up in the Webster family, which was living in Somerset County, Maryland, in 1910 and had moved to Baltimore by 1920.

Florence married Vernon L. Adams Sr. (1899–1974), son of John H. Adams and Chessie Fitchett Adams. Their children included Vernon L. Adams Jr. and Kenneth W. Adams. The 1930 census records their older son as Lee Adams, age six, while the 1940 census identifies him as Vernon L. Adams Jr., age sixteen.

After the death of Florence's mother, Addie Leola Daniel Webster, in 1922, Florence's younger brother Eugene Lee Webster became a member of her household. The 1930 census records Eugene, age eight, living with Florence, Vernon, and their son Lee in Baltimore. John H. Adams and Chessie Adams, Vernon's parents, were enumerated in the immediately following household.

The 1940 census records Florence and Vernon with their sons Vernon Jr. and Kenneth, along with Eugene Webster, then age eighteen. In 1950, Eugene, age twenty-eight, was still living with Florence and Vernon, together with their son Kenneth. These three census records document Eugene's residence with his older sister's family over a twenty-year period, although they do not establish that he lived there continuously.

The Adams family lived in Baltimore, Maryland. The 1950 census places them on Elsrode Avenue, and Florence's death certificate identifies her final residence as 6602 Elsrode Avenue. The family's precise residential history before 1950 remains under investigation.

Florence's husband Vernon died in 1974. Florence died on April 2, 1979, in Baltimore, Maryland, at age seventy-five. She was buried on April 5, 1979, at Moreland Memorial Park in Parkville, Maryland, where she shares a grave marker with Vernon.

Florence's 1979 death notice in The Evening Sun names her surviving siblings as Susan Kramer, Catherine Jackson, and James W. Webster. The notice also names Eugene L. Webster among her children, although the family records and earlier censuses establish that Eugene was her younger brother. This discrepancy is preserved for future research.
James Wilson Webster Sr. was born in 1920, the son of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. He died in 2005.
Mary Catherine Webster was born in 1916, the daughter of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. She died in 1995.

Maynard Snead Webster was born in 1900. He was the son of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. He was recorded as Maynard S. Webster, age nine, in the 1910 United States Federal Census in Somerset County, Maryland. He died in 1959.

Susie Catherine Webster, affectionately known as Sue, was born on October 22, 1902, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. She was the daughter of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel. According to family oral history, Sue was born with a twin sister, reportedly named Mary Catherine, who did not survive. The twin's identity and dates have not yet been independently verified.

The Webster family lived across the street from St. John's Methodist Episcopal Church at what is now 9883 Deal Island Road. The church dates to 1850 and was an important landmark in the community. The family's former house was reportedly demolished sometime in the late 1990s or early 2000s.

The Webster family moved from Deal Island to Baltimore around 1914, according to family history. The family lived at 2602 East Fayette Street. As a young woman, Sue worked as a telephone operator, reportedly beginning around 1918. Her employer and workplace location have not yet been independently verified.

Sue married Adam Johannes Krämer, whose surname was generally written Kramer in American records, on July 27, 1929, in Ellicott City, Howard County, Maryland. Their marriage was performed by H. D. Stewart of Emory Methodist Episcopal Church. According to family history, Sue and Adam were introduced by Lottie Smearman, identified as the daughter of Adam's aunt Loise Kramer. Sue and Adam had two children, Robert Adam Kramer and Bette Ann Kramer.

In 1938, Sue and Adam purchased a home in Dundalk, Baltimore County, Maryland. The family lived at 6902 Brentwood Avenue, a residence remembered by later generations of the family and documented in a family photograph. The 1940 and 1950 United States Federal Censuses record the Kramer household in the Baltimore area.

Sue devoted much of the period from 1936 through 1946 to raising her children at home. Around 1946, she began working in the cafeteria at Baltimore Pure Rye, where she served food until approximately 1957. She subsequently worked in the linen department at Hochschild Kohn's Eastpoint location from about 1957 until 1970 or 1971. These details of her employment are preserved in family history.

Sue spent her later years in Fairfax, Virginia. She died on January 1, 1993, at Fairfax Hospital in Falls Church, Virginia, at the age of 90. Her Virginia death certificate identifies a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm as the immediate cause of death. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore, Maryland, where her husband Adam was also buried.

William Gabriel Snead Webster was born on June 29, 1871 in Somerset County, Maryland. He was the son of Gabriel S. Webster and Susan A. Windsor, according to family research. During his adult life, he was commonly known as Gabriel Snead Webster or simply Snead Webster. His gravestone records his birth year as 1871, although his 1939 death certificate incorrectly reports a birth date of June 29, 1877.

On December 23, 1899, Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel applied for a marriage license in Somerset County, Maryland. The application recorded Snead as 27 years old and Addie as 18. By June 1900, they were living together as husband and wife in Tangier District, Somerset County, where they were enumerated in the United States Federal Census.

Snead and Addie established their family on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. On October 5, 1900, Snead acquired property on Deal Island through a deed involving Noah W. Webster, Rose A. Webster, John F. Webster, and Lucy B. Webster. The deed recorded a consideration of $115. Additional land records document the family's property transactions, including Addie's purchase of land from Lazarus B. Wilson and Annie B. Wilson in 1906 and a conveyance by Snead and Addie to Talmage D. Mister in 1909.

Snead and Addie were the parents of seven known children: Maynard Snead Webster (1900–1959), Susie Catherine Webster Kramer (1902–1993), Florence Melson Webster Adams (1904–1979), Charles Daniel Webster (1909–1960), Mary Catherine Webster Jackson (1916–1995), James Wilson Webster (1920–2005), and Eugene Lee Webster (1921–1998). The family lived on Deal Island during the early years of their marriage before relocating to Baltimore, Maryland. A surviving historical photograph documents their former home on Deal Island, which has since been demolished.

The Webster family was living in Baltimore by 1920. On April 26, 1922, Snead's wife Addie died at age 40, leaving several children still young. Her death certificate identifies Gabriel S. Webster as the informant. Family accounts describe the difficulties he faced caring for the younger children following her death. Later census records document different living arrangements among the children. In 1930, Charles and James Wilson Webster were living with their father, while Eugene Lee Webster was living with his older sister Florence and her husband Vernon L. Adams. The precise circumstances of these arrangements remain under investigation.

Gabriel later married Eloise Lonora Chiveral Reese, although the date of their marriage has not yet been established. His 1939 death certificate identifies Eloise as his wife and records his occupation as a carpenter, noting that he had retired from WPA employment.

William Gabriel Snead Webster died on April 17, 1939, at 200 North Glover Street in Baltimore, Maryland. His death certificate, completed using information supplied by Eloise, contains several discrepancies. It incorrectly identifies him as George Gabriel Snead Webster and names his parents as George Webster and Mary Katharine. Family research identifies his parents as Gabriel S. Webster and Susan A. Windsor. The certificate also reports a birth year of 1877, conflicting with the year 1871 inscribed on his gravestone, which was placed by his children.

Gabriel's death notice appeared in The Evening Sun of Baltimore on April 19, 1939. Funeral services were scheduled for April 20 at his residence on North Glover Street, followed by burial at Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore. His gravestone bears the inscription 'GABRIEL S. WEBSTER, 1871–1939, FATHER.'
Mary Catherine Wilson (1859–1910) is identified in FamilySearch family-tree research as the wife of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and the mother of seven children, including Addie Leola Daniel Webster.

Addie's 1922 Baltimore death certificate identifies her mother as Mary C. Wilson and records her birthplace as Somerset County, Maryland. This provides documentary evidence for Addie's maternal relationship.

Family-tree research identifies Mary as a daughter of Samuel David Wilson (1823–1914) and a sister of Lazarus Benjamin Wilson (1857–1922). In 1906, Lazarus and his wife Annie conveyed property on Deals Island, Maryland, to Mary's daughter Addie. The deed documents the transaction, while the precise family relationships require corroboration through additional records.
FamilySearch lists Mary's marriage to James Fairfax Daniel Sr. as December 16, 1875 or 1876. The marriage year remains uncertain pending examination of an original marriage record.

Susan A. Windsor, affectionately known as Susie, was born on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland, in 1843. Family research records her birth date as December 6, 1843, and identifies her parents as William Windsor and Susan Jones. These details remain subject to confirmation through historical records.

On December 20, 1865, Susan married Gabriel S. Webster in Somerset County, Maryland. Their marriage is documented in the county marriage register. Family research identifies their children as Anna Elizabeth 'Lizzie' Webster (1868–1940) and William Gabriel Snead Webster (1871–1939).
Gabriel S. Webster died in 1871, approximately six years after their marriage. Susan subsequently married William Jacob Webster (1836–1910). The date of their marriage has not yet been established.
Susan's granddaughter, Susie Catherine Webster Kramer (1902–1993), daughter of William Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel, was named in her honor, according to family history.

Susan died on February 10, 1911, at Deal Island, Maryland, at the reported age of 68. Her death certificate identifies her as Susie Webster and records pneumonia following la grippe as the cause of death. Her son, Snead Webster, provided the information for the certificate.

Susan was buried on February 12, 1911, at Saint John's Cemetery on Deal Island, beside her second husband, William Jacob Webster, who died in 1910. Their adjacent gravestones identify them as 'MOTHER' and 'FATHER,' respectively.

Gabriel Snead Webster was born in approximately 1822 in Maryland. On June 27, 1849, he married Mary A. Jones, identified in family research as Mary Adeline Jones, in Somerset County, Maryland. Their marriage is documented in the county marriage register. Following Mary's reported death in 1863, Gabriel married Susan A. Windsor on December 20, 1865.

In August 1863, Gabriel S. Webster appeared in the United States Civil War draft registration for Tangier District, Somerset County, Maryland. He was recorded as a 38-year-old boatman born in Maryland. His inclusion establishes that he was registered as subject to military duty but does not establish that he served in the Union Army. The age recorded in this document suggests a birth around 1824–1825, somewhat later than the 1822 birth year currently associated with him.
Gabriel S. Webster and Susan A. Windsor married on December 20, 1865, according to their marriage record.

Gabriel and Susan were the parents of Anna Elizabeth Webster Todd (1868–1940) and William Gabriel Snead Webster (1871–1939). Anna's 1940 Maryland death certificate identifies her father as Snead Webster and her mother as Susie Windsor.

Tragedy struck the Webster family in September 1871 when Gabriel Snead Webster and two of his sons died of typhoid fever within five days. A contemporary newspaper reported that a younger son died on Thursday, September 7, followed by Gabriel and his son Snead on Monday, September 11. Gabriel and Snead died within hours of each other. Family research identifies the two sons as Elmer Webster (1860–1871) and Newton Snead Webster (1855–1871), respectively. The newspaper describes the family as residents of Deal's Island, Somerset County, Maryland.

Leah White Webster was born on April 27, possibly in 1776. Her gravestone appears to record this birth date, although the final digit of the year is difficult to distinguish and may indicate 1770. The 1850 United States Census records her age as 65, suggesting a later birth year. Her exact birth year therefore remains uncertain.

On September 6, 1808, Leah White married John Webster. Their marriage is documented in a historical marriage-register listing associated with Coventry Parish, Rehobeth, Somerset County, Maryland. Family research identifies her husband as John Gabriel Webster III (1784–1844), although the marriage record itself identifies him only as John Webster.

In the 1850 United States Census, Leah Webster was recorded in Dames Quarter District, Somerset County, Maryland, in the same household as Snead Webster, age 23, and Adaline Webster, age 20. Family research identifies Snead Webster as her son Gabriel Snead Webster (1822–1871), but the census does not specify household relationships.
Leah died on January 1, 1857, according to her gravestone. She was buried at Saint Johns Cemetery on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland.
John Webster married Leah White on September 6, 1808, in Coventry Parish, Somerset County, Maryland, according to the parish marriage register.
FamilySearch identifies him as John Gabriel Webster III (1784–1844). His middle name, suffix, and birth and death years have not yet been independently verified.
FamilySearch identifies John and Leah as the parents of Gabriel Snead Webster (1822–1871), but this relationship requires additional historical documentation.

Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma, was born on October 30, 1877, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland. Her 1939 death certificate identifies her parents as James Daniel and Mary C. Wilson, corresponding to James Fairfax Daniel and Mary Catherine Wilson.

Emma married William E. Kelly, whose surname also appears as Kelley in historical records. William was born in 1870, according to their shared gravestone. The date and location of their marriage have not yet been established.

By 1910, Emma and William were living with their children at 2014 Walbrook Avenue in Baltimore, Maryland. Emma's father, James Fairfax Daniel, lived nearby at 2010 Walbrook Avenue. The neighboring residences document the geographic closeness of two generations of the Daniel family after leaving their roots on Deal Island.

Emma was living at 520 Eutaw Street in Baltimore at the time of her death on September 16, 1939. Her death certificate records her cause of death as carcinoma of the uterus. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore, where she shares a gravestone with William E. Kelly, who died in 1950.

FamilySearch identifies Isadora Franklin Daniel (1880–1967) as a daughter of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and Mary Catherine Wilson. Her reported birth and death years and parentage have not yet been independently verified through historical records.

FamilySearch identifies Katherine W. Daniel (1883–1944) as a daughter of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and Mary Catherine Wilson. Her reported birth and death years and parentage have not yet been independently verified through historical records.

FamilySearch identifies James Fairfax Daniel Jr. (1885–1915) as a son of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and Mary Catherine Wilson. His reported birth and death years and parentage have not yet been independently verified through historical records.

FamilySearch identifies Anna Wilson Daniel (1887–1957) as a daughter of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and Mary Catherine Wilson. Her reported birth and death years and parentage have not yet been independently verified through historical records.

FamilySearch identifies Wilson Bounds Daniel (1897–1918) as a son of James Fairfax Daniel Sr. and Mary Catherine Wilson. His reported birth and death years and parentage have not yet been independently verified through historical records.

James Travers Daniel was born on February 14, 1830, according to his gravestone, and spent his life in the Wenona area of Deal Island, Somerset County, Maryland. He died there on February 10, 1902, just four days before his seventy-second birthday. His death certificate confirms his death date, although the age recorded on the certificate differs slightly from the dates inscribed on his gravestone.

James received his early education on Deal Island before entering Dickinson College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, in 1848, at approximately eighteen years of age. He attended for two years but did not graduate. According to Portrait and Biographical Record of the Eastern Shore (1898), he established a good academic record during his time at the college.

James cultivated a 20-acre farm in Wenona and operated a mercantile business near the Wenona Post Office. The 1898 biographical account described him as a businessman who adapted his activities to the needs of the surrounding community and took an interest in the welfare of its residents. His 1902 death certificate also records his occupation as a mail driver.

James was active in public affairs and supported the prohibition movement. He served as a judge of the Somerset County Orphans' Court from 1876 to 1880. According to the biographical account, he was nominated for positions in both the Maryland legislature and state senate but declined the nominations. His obituary, published in a newspaper dispatch to the Baltimore Sun, described him as a prominent Prohibitionist who had frequently represented his party in state and county conventions and had been considered for the Maryland State Senate on the Prohibition ticket.

James's brother William Daniel (1826–1897) was a Maryland attorney, state legislator, and prominent prohibition advocate who became the Prohibition Party's nominee for vice president of the United States in the 1884 presidential election, running alongside John P. St. John of Kansas. The Baltimore Sun identified William as James's brother in an article published on August 1, 1892.

Religion and community service were important parts of James's life. He was a member of the Methodist Episcopal Church, serving as a steward and trustee, and was a local preacher for fifteen years or more. He was also associated with the Heptasophs, a fraternal organization.

James married Louisa E. Rowe on January 6, 1855, in Somerset County, Maryland. Following her death, he married Elizabeth Andrews, who was also known as Lizzie Daniel. His obituary confirms that he married twice and reports that he was survived by his widow and thirteen children. The 1880 United States Census records James T. Daniel, age 50, in Deal Island in a household that also included James F. Daniel, age 24.

James's death certificate identifies his father as Travers Daniel and appears to identify his mother as Molly Wallace. These names remain subject to further verification before the parent-child relationships are formally established in the family archive.

James died at his residence in Wenona on February 10, 1902. His gravestone stands in St. John's Methodist Church Cemetery on Deal Island. Nellie Wallace Armstrong, who was approximately ten years old at the time of his death, later remembered him as a very fine man.

William Edward Kelly was born on April 6, 1870, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland, according to the United States Social Security Numerical Identification Files (NUMIDENT). An October 1942 Social Security record identifies him by his full name and records his birthplace.
William married Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma. Her 1939 death certificate identifies her husband as William E. Kelley, reflecting an alternate spelling of the family surname.
By 1910, William and Emma were living with their children at 2014 Walbrook Avenue in Baltimore, Maryland, near Emma's father, James Fairfax Daniel, who lived at 2010 Walbrook Avenue.

William died on September 27, 1950, in Cambridge, Maryland. His death notice, published in The Baltimore Sun on September 30, 1950, identified him as the husband of the late Emma L. Kelly, née Daniels, and announced funeral services in Baltimore followed by interment at Woodlawn Cemetery. William and Emma share a gravestone at Woodlawn Cemetery bearing their names and years of birth and death.

Edward Maynard Kelly was born on October 3, 1898, on Deal Island in Somerset County, Maryland, according to family tree information recorded on Ancestry. He is identified as a son of William Edward Kelly and Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma.
Edward's family later lived in Baltimore, Maryland. His parents were recorded at 2014 Walbrook Avenue in 1910, near his maternal grandfather, James Fairfax Daniel.
Ancestry family tree information gives Edward's death year as 1966. His exact death date and place remain to be verified.

William Daniel Kelly was born on October 4, 1900, in Somerset County, Maryland, according to Ancestry family tree information. He was identified as a son of William Edward Kelly and Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma.

William's parents later resided at 2014 Walbrook Avenue in Baltimore, Maryland, according to the 1910 United States Census. His maternal grandfather, James Fairfax Daniel, lived nearby at 2010 Walbrook Avenue.
Ancestry family tree information records William's death year as 1972. His exact death date and place remain to be verified.

James Dryden Kelly Sr. was born on January 7, 1903, in Maryland, according to Ancestry family tree information. He is identified as a son of William Edward Kelly and Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma.
In 1910, James's parents lived at 2014 Walbrook Avenue in Baltimore, Maryland, near his maternal grandfather, James Fairfax Daniel, who resided at 2010 Walbrook Avenue.
Ancestry family tree information records James's death year as 1973. His exact death date and place remain to be verified.
George Roscoe Kelly was born in 1910, according to Ancestry family tree information. He is identified as a son of William Edward Kelly and Louisa Elizabeth Daniel, known as Emma.
